newsitem.title: USA: Fla. insurance chief rejects State Farm rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Fla. insurance chief rejects State Farm rate hike.

text.p: Florida Insurance Commissioner Bill Nelson said Tuesday he would reject State Farm's request for a 23.4 percent statewide rate hike for homeowner's insurance.

"I'm going back to Tallahassee this afternoon and I'm going to reject this rate increase," Nelson told the Dade County Commission. State Farm, the nation's largest personal property insurer, sought the rate hike last week.

Nelson also pledged to set up a statewide task force to ensure that homeowners are receiving the credits and discounts they are entitled to under policies that make special provisions when homes have safety featueres such as hurricane shutters.
Nelson spoke to the commission in support of a Dade County ordinance urging the legislature to help make homeowner's insurance available and affordable in areas ravaged by Hurricane Andrew.

Nelson said that insurance companies had returned to Florida, creating competition that resulted in rate cuts for auto and workers' compensation policies. However, he said, "It is homeowners that are still a paralyzed insurance market."
Nelson said he would promote efforts to bring additional insurance companies into Florida in order to help phase out the state-run home insurance pool known as the Joint Underwriting Association.
The pool was created after Hurricane Andrew's devastating August 1992 passage through south Florida.
The storm caused more than $20 billion in damage, causing some insurance companies to fold and others to drop customers in a bid to lessen their risk exposure in the state.
The pool was intended to ensure that property owners had access to insurance when the private insurance market crumbled.

Nelson also pledged to fight efforts by actuaries and insurance companies to create a new computerized risk model that he said was erroneous and would increase premium rates by 1,182 percent in Dade County.
Nelson further said he would implement a statewide rate cut averaging 3.4 percent for homeowners insured through the JUA.
